stem.text: The height H of the water in a tank, in centimeters, connected to a reservoir whose water stands at 55 centimeters moves toward the reservoir height at a rate proportional to the difference between the reservoir height and H. At time \( t = 0 \) hours, \( H = 80 \). Using k for the positive constant of proportionality, write a differential equation for H as a function of t and state the initial condition.

worked_solution.text: The dependent variable is H and the independent variable is t in hours, so the rate is \( \frac{dH}{dt} \).

Proportional to the difference means a constant multiple of it. With k positive, \( k(55 - H) \) is positive when H is below 55 and negative when it is above, so H moves down toward 55 from its starting value.
The equation is \( \frac{dH}{dt} = k\left(55 - H\right) \), and the initial condition, stated separately, is \( H(0) = 80 \).

options.label: \( \frac{dH}{dt} = k\left(H - 55\right) \), with \( H(0) = 80 \)
options.derivation: the difference written as H minus the level, which with k positive drives H away from 55

options.label: \( \frac{dH}{dt} = k\left(55 - 80\right) \), with \( H(0) = 80 \)
options.derivation: the initial value 80 substituted for H inside the equation, so the rate becomes a constant

options.label: \( \frac{dH}{dt} = 55 - H \), with \( H(0) = 80 \)
options.derivation: proportional read as equal, so the constant k never appears
